I think it’s a skill issue. 

If the parents lack the skills and knowledge on how to leverage these tools then it becomes an issue. 

The safe way is for the gov to do what they are doing. 

However it will create an even broader divide, and that hurts the very fabric of society even more. 

Kids don’t need AI as much as they don’t need tablets or phones or TV’s. 

We have very strict rules around screen time, and tablet use in our home, but if it was not for the iPad my kids would not have read and write before the age of 4 in 3 languages. 

My daughters and I use AI not daily but definitely weekly, for all sorts of things. But I’d argue that 80% plus of the use is for educational purposes and information gathering, so we can have nuanced conversations about how things work. 

And they CONSTANTLY hear us talk back to the AI, telling it how it’s wrong and flawed in it’s logic. The kids have soaked this up like sponges, they are very critical to what ever the AI says. I think they have more trust in Bluey than Gemini or Chat. 

Putting the kids outside of tech is great, they don’t need it. The reason there is a YT kids pandemic and dopamine hurt kids world wide is because of neglect from parents, not kids. 

Kids have no idea these things exist, we put them infront of them, so while I’m personally not thrilled with this direction, because of the widening of gaps, and lack of understanding in what direction the world is going, I can see the benefits and give the benefit of the doubt. 

parents are still allowed to tech their kids whatever they like at home.

It's DLSS 5 (generative neural upscaling) essentially using diffusion technology to upscale each frame in real-time, using the same technologies that are being used to generate AI images. But it uses the input from the base render of the GPU and then use small on card models, to upscale frame by frame before you see it, at +300 fps. Runs on a single 50-series chip.
